patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient presents to the emergency department with abdominal pain and reports being 10 weeks pregnant. She has a history of constipation, anxiety, and substance abuse. The patient is not currently on any medications.

Secondary_Symptoms: Emotional distress upon learning of a spontaneous abortion

patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Details on social history not provided, but the doctor should inquire about current life stressors, support systems, and substance use.

questions: Are you currently pregnant or could you be pregnant (when was your last menstrual period)?
Do you have any vaginal bleeding or unusual vaginal discharge right now, and if so what color/amount?
Do you have any fever or chills, and if yes what temperature?
Where exactly is the abdominal pain located (e.g., right lower, left lower, upper abdomen, or around the belly button), and is it constant or coming in waves?
Are you having any hearing voices or intrusive thoughts that tell you to hurt yourself or someone else?
Have you had any periods of unusually elevated or irritable mood with decreased need for sleep lasting at least 4 days (e.g., feeling “amped up,” more talkative, racing thoughts, or risky behavior)?
Have you had these voices or intrusive thoughts (or any other psychotic symptoms) for more than a month continuously?
Have the voices/intrusive thoughts been present every day since they started, and are they occurring when you’re fully awake (not just while falling asleep or waking up)?
Have you had any periods of depressed mood or loss of interest lasting at least 2 weeks since these symptoms began (and were they present most of the day, nearly every day)?
Have you had any period of depression (sadness or loss of interest) lasting at least 2 weeks, separate from the voices, either before or after the hallucinations started?
answers: Doctor: Are you currently pregnant or could you be pregnant—when was your last menstrual period? Patient: I’m not pregnant as far as I know, but I don’t feel sure—my last menstrual period started about three weeks ago.
Patient: No, I’m not having any vaginal bleeding or unusual discharge right now—nothing out of the ordinary.

Patient: I don’t have any fever or chills, and I haven’t measured a temperature recently because I’ve been feeling normal physically. I’ve mainly been dealing with the voices and intrusive thoughts, not any illness symptoms.
Patient: I don’t have abdominal pain at all—my main issues are the voices and intrusive thoughts, and I’m not having any pain that comes and goes.
“Doctor, yes—the voices are discussing me in third person and they’re encouraging me to hurt myself. I’ve been having intrusive thoughts too, and it’s been hard to concentrate around them.”

Patient: I don’t think my mood has been unusually elevated, and I haven’t had a decreased need for sleep—I’m mostly just overwhelmed by the voices, the intrusive thoughts, and it’s been affecting my focus. I haven’t noticed racing thoughts or risky behavior; it feels more like I can’t quiet my mind.

Doctor: Have you had these voices or intrusive thoughts (or any other psychotic symptoms) for more than a month continuously? Patient: No, it’s been about a week since it started, right after my father died. It hasn’t been continuous for a full month.
Patient: Yes, they’ve been there pretty much every day since they started, and they happen when I’m fully awake. I can’t seem to get away from them, even when I’m trying to focus on other things.

“Doctor, I haven’t had loss of interest for at least two weeks, but I feel very distressed and my mood drops because the voices and intrusive thoughts won’t stop. It’s mostly the voices and concentration problems that are dominating most of my day.”

Doctor, I haven’t had sadness or loss of interest for a full two weeks separate from the voices—I’m distressed, but it seems like it comes mainly because the voices and intrusive thoughts won’t stop. I don’t feel “down” in a way that lasts that long on its own; it’s mostly the mental noise that’s driving everything.
